stem: Which of the following are true characteristics of deliberative agents, as distinguished from reactive agents? (Select 2)

options.text: They maintain and reason over an internal model of the task or environment
They consider the consequences of candidate actions before committing to one
They always respond faster than reactive agents
They cannot be implemented using large language models

explanation.why_correct: Maintaining an internal model and weighing the consequences of candidate actions before acting are the two defining characteristics that separate deliberative agents from reactive, direct-mapping ones.

why_incorrect.C: Deliberative agents are typically SLOWER than reactive agents due to the added planning/lookahead computation, not faster.
why_incorrect.D: Large language models are commonly used to implement the reasoning/planning core of deliberative agents; there is no incompatibility between LLMs and deliberative design.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Deliberative agents are defined by internal modeling and consequence-weighing before acting -- not by speed, which is actually a cost of this approach, not a benefit.

stem: Which of the following environment/task properties would favor choosing a reactive agent architecture over a deliberative one? (Select 2)

options.text: Situations are mostly familiar and recurring, matching well-known patterns
The task requires balancing many competing constraints to find an optimal multi-step plan
The environment is highly novel and rarely repeats the same situation twice

explanation.why_correct: Tight latency requirements and mostly familiar, recurring situations are exactly the conditions where a reactive architecture's speed advantage pays off without sacrificing much robustness, since there's little need for costly deliberation.

why_incorrect.C: Balancing many competing constraints for an optimal multi-step plan is a textbook case favoring deliberative architecture, which can weigh alternatives, rather than reactive matching.
why_incorrect.D: A highly novel environment with rarely-repeating situations is poorly served by a fixed rule set, favoring deliberative reasoning that can handle unfamiliar cases rather than reactive pattern matching.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Reactive design fits fast, familiar, recurring situations; deliberative design fits novel, complex, constraint-heavy situations -- match the architecture to these task properties.

stem: Which of the following correctly describe how a well-designed hybrid agent architecture typically operates? (Select 2)

options.text: It attempts a fast reactive-style response first, escalating to deliberation only when needed
It runs the full deliberative process on every single decision, regardless of complexity
It uses some signal (e.g. low confidence, detected novelty, high stakes) to decide when to escalate
It requires exactly two different underlying language models, one for each layer

explanation.why_correct: A hybrid architecture's value comes from trying the fast path first and using some escalation signal (low confidence, novelty, stakes) to decide when the slower deliberative path is actually needed, avoiding the cost of full deliberation on every decision.

why_incorrect.B: Running full deliberation on every decision defeats the purpose of a hybrid design, which specifically aims to avoid that cost for the common/easy cases.
why_incorrect.D: A hybrid architecture does not require two distinct models; the same underlying model can serve both a quick low-effort mode and an extended reasoning mode, depending on how the system invokes it.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Hybrid architectures are defined by selective escalation based on some signal, not by running every decision through the expensive path or requiring separate models per layer.

stem: Which of the following systems would be reasonably classified as reactive agents? (Select 2)

options.text: A thermostat that turns heating on below a set temperature and off above another
A keyword-matching FAQ bot that returns a canned answer when it detects a known phrase
A trip-planning system that evaluates dozens of candidate multi-city itineraries against budget constraints
A research assistant that decomposes a complex question into sub-questions and plans how to answer each

explanation.why_correct: Both the thermostat and the keyword-matching FAQ bot map current input directly to an action via fixed condition-action rules, with no internal planning or lookahead -- the defining trait of reactive agents.

why_incorrect.C: Evaluating many candidate plans against constraints before choosing one is deliberative behavior, involving an internal model and consequence-weighing, not a direct reactive mapping.
why_incorrect.D: Decomposing a problem into sub-questions and planning how to answer each is explicit multi-step planning, characteristic of a deliberative agent, not a reactive one.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Direct input-to-action mappings with no internal modeling or lookahead are reactive; anything involving explicit planning or weighing of multiple candidate approaches is deliberative.
